subject: dsa
title: Valid Anagram
summary: Count every letter in s, then subtract one for each letter in t. If every count lands back at zero, t is a rearrangement of s.
problem: Return true if t is an anagram of s — the same letters with the same counts, just reordered.

steps.caption: An anagram uses the exact same letters the same number of times. If the lengths differ it's an instant no; otherwise tally s and cancel with t.
Count the letters of s = "cat": one c, one a, one t.
Now sweep t = "act", subtracting one per letter. First 'a': it's in the map, drop its count to 0.
Next 'c': also present, drop it to 0.
Last 't': present, drop it to 0. A missing letter or a count going negative here would mean 'not an anagram'.
Every count is back to zero, so t spent exactly the letters s had. "act" is an anagram of "cat" — return true.
